journey.title: Early Childhood
journey.tagline: The beginning of a curious mind.
intro: Cheistha was born in Bareilly on 10 August 1990 into an Army family.
highlights: Born in Bareilly, 10 August 1990
Born into an Army family

journey.title: Primary School
journey.tagline: First lessons, first friendships, first wonders.
intro: She completed her early schooling in Army schools at Srinagar, Mhow, and Bhatinda.
highlights: Army schools at Srinagar, Mhow and Bhatinda

journey.title: School Years
journey.tagline: Formative years of learning and friendship.
intro: She later attended Emerald Heights Public School, Indore, and the Convent of Jesus and Mary, New Delhi.

During her school years, she was an active participant in debating, painting, and writing, including poetry, with many of her works published in relevant sections of newspapers. Remarkably, she also cleared the Inter exam of JJ School of Arts while in class 9.
highlights: Emerald Heights Public School, Indore
Convent of Jesus and Mary, New Delhi
Debating, painting, writing and poetry
Cleared the Inter exam of JJ School of Arts in class 9

journey.title: College Graduation
intro: She pursued her undergraduate studies in Economics (Hons) at Venkateshwara College, New Delhi.

Her critical thinking and socially conscious entrepreneurial skills began to shine early. She co-founded Feed India and interned with the Centre for Civil Society (CCS), where she researched and wrote on topics including “Vigilanting the Vigilance.” She also presented a paper at a conference at Harvard during this period.
highlights: Economics (Hons), Venkateshwara College, New Delhi
Co-founded Feed India
Presented a paper at a conference at Harvard

professional.title: Centre for Civil Society
professional.tagline: Early research and writing on governance and accountability.
intro: An internship with the Centre for Civil Society (CCS) gave early expression to her analytical instincts and her interest in governance and accountability. There she researched and wrote on subjects such as “Vigilanting the Vigilance,” and it was in this period that she also presented a paper at a conference at Harvard.
highlights: Research and writing, including “Vigilanting the Vigilance”
Focus on governance and accountability
Presented a paper at a conference at Harvard

professional.title: UIDAI
professional.tagline: Founding team of Aadhaar, and the first Aadhaar number in the country.
intro: Cheistha then joined the founding team of Aadhaar, earning the distinction of being assigned the first Aadhaar number in the country due to her contributions in writing the process document as the youngest team member.
highlights: Founding team of Aadhaar
Assigned the first Aadhaar number in the country
Youngest team member; wrote the process document

professional.title: McKinsey & Company
professional.tagline: A year as an analyst, after choosing to stay in India.
intro: Although selected for a master’s in public policy at LSE with a full scholarship, she chose to stay in India, joining McKinsey as an analyst for a year, followed by the Young India Fellowship (YIF) as a fully paid fellow.
highlights: Analyst for one year
Chose India over a fully funded LSE master’s offer

professional.title: Young India Fellowship
professional.tagline: A fully paid fellow remembered for compassion and a ready-to-help attitude.
intro: Although selected for a master’s in public policy at LSE with a full scholarship, she chose to stay in India, joining McKinsey as an analyst for a year, followed by the Young India Fellowship (YIF) as a fully paid fellow. Her compassion and “ready-to-help” attitude left a lasting impression at YIF. After her passing, YIF compiled a booklet containing her quotes from her time there. Even after graduating, she remained a regular speaker for new YIF batches. In one of her speeches, she profoundly noted that her life principle was to create something that lasts far beyond herself.
During this period, she also earned a PG diploma from the University of Pennsylvania.
highlights: Fully paid fellow
YIF compiled a booklet of her quotes after her passing
Regular speaker for new YIF batches
PG diploma from the University of Pennsylvania

professional.title: Planning Commission
professional.tagline: Senior Advisor working concurrently with the Ministry of HRD.
intro: After YIF, she worked concurrently in the Planning Commission and Ministry of HRD as a Senior Advisor, engaging with leading figures in Government and academia.
highlights: Senior Advisor, Planning Commission and Ministry of HRD
Engaged with leading figures in Government and academia

professional.title: University of Chicago
professional.tagline: From the Delhi Centre and the Anubhav Leadership Series to the Harris School.
intro: She subsequently joined the University of Chicago Centre in Delhi, where she developed a deep interest in Organizational Behaviour and Leadership. She founded the Anubhav Leadership Series, which became immensely popular and has since been renamed the Cheistha Kochhar Anubhav Series. During her tenure, she successfully convinced the Government and UChicago to conduct courses at Chicago for mid-career bureaucrats, sending a batch under this initiative with DOPT.

Cheistha then joined the Harris School of the University of Chicago as a full-time resident student in the MAIDP program. She was awarded a full scholarship and received the Harris Fellowship, Clinton Fellowship, and TATA Memorial Scholarship. Her interest in Organizational Behaviour, particularly Nudge Theory, deepened as she interacted not only with Harris faculty but also with Nobel Laureates on campus, building lifelong professional relationships. She also served as a TA at the adjoining Booth School of Management.
Her work extended to AI applications, which she applied in her research and writings, and she travelled extensively across neighbouring countries.
highlights: Founded the Anubhav Leadership Series, now the Cheistha Kochhar Anubhav Series
Sent a batch of mid-career bureaucrats to Chicago with DOPT
MAIDP, Harris School, with a full scholarship
Harris Fellowship, Clinton Fellowship, TATA Memorial Scholarship
TA at the Booth School of Management

professional.title: NITI Aayog
professional.tagline: Founder of India’s first Nudge Unit and the Global South’s first Behavioural Insights Unit.
intro: When COVID struck, she returned to India and joined NITI Aayog as part of an embedded team from the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation (BMGF) as a Senior Consultant, working directly in the CEO’s office. She established the Behavioural Insights Unit (BIU) in NITI Aayog, the first in the Global South, and founded India’s first Nudge Unit, passionately applying behavioural science to national projects. She contributed to numerous interventions, including the PM’s flagship LIFE project, organized a mega event at Kevadia, Gujarat, and conducted a global high-level conference chaired by the PM, attended by Heads of State, IMF, World Bank, and multiple Nobel Laureates. She also delivered several presentations to the PM on these initiatives.
highlights: Senior Consultant, embedded BMGF team, CEO’s office
Established the Behavioural Insights Unit, the first in the Global South
Founded India’s first Nudge Unit
Contributed to the PM’s flagship LIFE project
Mega event at Kevadia, Gujarat
Global high-level conference chaired by the PM

professional.title: London School of Economics
professional.tagline: A fully funded PhD on Nudge Theory implementation, with a focus on India.
intro: Cheistha got married in December 2022. In September 2023, she joined LSE for a fully funded PhD programme in the Organisational Behaviour Department, focusing on Nudge Theory implementation with a particular emphasis on India. Her dedication led to her being assigned TA responsibilities within three months, nominated to co-present at an international conference in Copenhagen in July 2024, and concurrently appointed as a Senior Consultant at UChicago to establish a Nudge Unit with a focus on India. She also advised BIT informally on the same subject. By this stage, she was recognized as one of the few experts in implementing Nudge Theory and was co-authoring two books, one with Dr. Lourdes Sosa at LSE and another with Ranjan Daniels of University of Chicago.
highlights: Fully funded PhD, Organisational Behaviour Department
TA responsibilities within three months
Co-presenter, international conference in Copenhagen, July 2024
Senior Consultant at UChicago, establishing a Nudge Unit for India
Co-authoring two books, with Dr. Lourdes Sosa and Ranjan Daniels

initiatives.title: 1st Cheistha Kochhar Memorial Lecture
initiatives.tagline: The inaugural memorial lecture on the future of behavioural science.
initiatives.institution: University of Delhi | Department of Psychology & Cheistha Kochhar Nudge Centre
initiatives.description: Organised with the Department of Psychology, University of Delhi, the inaugural memorial lecture featured Biju Dominic discussing the future of behavioural science in a smartphone-first world and Cheistha's vision for digital-age nudging.

initiatives.title: BRICS CCI WE Global Women Icon Award
initiatives.tagline: A special leadership lecture and a posthumous honour for exceptional contributions to behavioural science and public policy.
initiatives.institution: BRICS CCI WE: Global Women Leadership Programme 2025 & Annual Women's Summit 2026
initiatives.description: Hosted by the BRICS CCI Women Empowerment Vertical, a special lecture on Nudge Theory in Leadership at the Global Women Leadership Programme 2025 explored how empathy, purpose and behavioural insights can transform leadership and workplace culture while honouring Cheistha's pioneering contributions. Cheistha was further posthumously honoured with the Global Women Icon Award at the BRICS CCI WE Annual Women's Summit 2026 for her exceptional contributions to behavioural science, innovation and public policy.

initiatives.title: Cheistha Kochhar Master of Research Prize
initiatives.tagline: An annual prize celebrating excellence in research and academic integrity.
initiatives.institution: London School of Economics and Political Science (LSE)
initiatives.description: Established by the Department of Management, LSE, this annual prize recognises the highest-performing MRes student and celebrates excellence in research and academic integrity.

initiatives.title: Annual Memorial Lecture & People Speak Memorial Debate
initiatives.tagline: An annual lecture connecting campus with careers, and a premier debating tournament celebrating fearless expression.
initiatives.institution: Sri Venkateswara College, University of Delhi
initiatives.description:
Hosted by the Economics Association, the Annual Memorial Lecture connects campus with careers through insights on leadership, learning and purpose.

Held in Cheistha's memory, the People Speak Memorial Debate is a premier debating tournament celebrating critical thinking, reasoned discourse and fearless expression.

initiatives.title: Behavioural Confluence
initiatives.tagline: Public Policy Day bringing together researchers and policymakers.
initiatives.description:
Public Policy Day at Behavioural Confluence honours Cheistha's legacy by bringing together researchers and policymakers to discuss behavioural science and governance.

The event grows out of the Foundation's long-term partnership with CHRIST (Deemed to be University), promoting behavioural science through lectures, workshops, research programmes and the Cheistha Kochhar Nudge Lecture Series.

initiatives.title: Strategic Partnership with JIBS
initiatives.tagline: An MoU to advance behavioural science, and an annual rolling trophy for innovative, scalable projects.
initiatives.institution: Jindal Institute of Behavioural Sciences, O.P. Jindal Global University
initiatives.description: An MoU to advance behavioural science through collaborative research, leadership development, student engagement and community impact. The partnership also instituted the Cheistha Kochhar Rolling Trophy at the JIBS Nudge Lab Competition, an annual trophy recognising innovative behavioural science projects that offer scalable solutions to real-world challenges.

initiatives.title: Cheistha Kochhar Good Samaritan Award
initiatives.tagline: An annual award recognising courage, compassion and public service.
initiatives.description: An annual award recognising extraordinary acts of courage, compassion and public service while supporting recipients to expand their impact.

initiatives.title: Cheistha Kochhar Anubhav Lecture Series
initiatives.tagline: Equipping grassroots changemakers with leadership and public policy skills.
initiatives.description: Originally conceptualised by Cheistha and renamed in her honour, the series equips grassroots changemakers with leadership and public policy skills.

initiatives.title: Cheistha Kochhar Merit Scholarship
initiatives.tagline: Merit scholarships recognising the effort and achievement of schoolchildren.
initiatives.description:
The Cheistha Kochhar Merit Scholarship recognises students at Manak School for their dedication and achievement in their studies, with certificates presented to the scholars in the presence of their classmates.

The scholarship reflects Cheistha's lifelong belief in education as the foundation of opportunity, and the Foundation's commitment to encouraging young learners at the very beginning of their journey.

initiatives.title: Cheistha Kochhar Debate & Essay Writing Competition
initiatives.tagline: A debate and essay writing competition held in her memory at her own school.
initiatives.description:
Held in the fond memory of Cheistha Kochhar, an alumna of Army Public School, Mhow, the competition brings together young debaters and essayists in English and Hindi. The English and Hindi debate is open to Classes IX to XII, while the English essay writing contest runs in two categories, for Classes VI to VIII and Classes IX to XII.

The school remembers Cheistha as a student known for her academic prowess and excellence in co-curricular activities, a trail-blazing scholar and a visionary leader.

initiatives.title: Cheistha Kochhar Best Female Post Graduate Student Award
initiatives.tagline: Honouring the best female postgraduate student in engineering and research.
initiatives.description:
The Cheistha Kochhar Best Female Post Graduate Student Award was unveiled at the Army Institute of Technology, Pune, during the IEEE International Conference on Nexus of Digitization, Intelligence & Applications (ICNDIA-2026), held at the Institute on 18 and 19 September 2026. The award is presented as a rolling trophy carrying Cheistha's portrait, recognising a young woman who excels in engineering and research.

The unveiling was followed by a keynote address by Lt Gen Dr S P Kochhar, Cheistha's father, on the evolution of India's telecommunication and networking infrastructure. He also joined the release of the conference proceedings.

The conference brought together academicians, researchers, industry professionals and technology experts to exchange perspectives on digitization, intelligence, AI, cybersecurity and emerging applications. The award carries Cheistha's belief that rigour and opportunity should go hand in hand, and the Foundation's commitment to encouraging women to lead in technology and research.

initiatives.title: Cheistha Kochhar Nudge Awards
initiatives.tagline: National awards for applied behavioural science creating social impact.
initiatives.description: National awards recognising individuals, teams and organisations applying behavioural science to create measurable social impact across India.

Working with institutions on evidence-led policy, evaluation and public-interest research.
Merit scholarships and school programmes that help students continue their studies with dignity.
Mentoring and leadership initiatives, including collaborations with women's leadership platforms.
Annual lectures and awards with universities and institutions that keep her ideas in public conversation.
Open to organisations, institutions and foundations seeking partners for philanthropic and social-impact work.
